ISNI (International Standard Name Identifier)

ISNI, the International Standard Name Identifier, is the ISO certified global standard number, ISO 27729, for identifying the contributors to creative works and those active in their distribution, from researchers, inventors and writers to performers, producers, publishers and aggregators; the leesharks.com authorship census holds it as a registry whose unit is a number assigned to a public identity: an individual, a pseudonym, or an organization or group. Encyclopedic and book-trade accounts give its object as the public identities of contributors to media content such as books, television programmes and newspaper articles, a creator, author or contributor identified by a unique number. The number has sixteen characters, fifteen digits followed by a check character that may be a digit or the letter X, computed by the ISO/IEC 7064 MOD 11-2 algorithm, and it is often displayed in four blocks. It was developed under the International Organization for Standardization as Draft International Standard 27729, under technical committee 46, subcommittee 9, and the valid standard was published on 15 March 2012; it belongs to the family of international standard identifiers that includes DOI, ISAN, ISBN, ISRC, ISSN and ISWC.

The agency's mission is to assign a persistent unique number "to the public name(s)" of a researcher, inventor, writer, artist, performer or publisher, to resolve the problem of name ambiguity in search and discovery, and to diffuse each number across the repertoires of the global supply chain "so that every published work can be unambiguously attributed to its creator wherever that work is described." With the number, named entities that might otherwise be confused are told apart: trading partners use it in metadata to distinguish authors with the same or similar names, and the data about names collected across the media industries can be linked through it to the other identifiers used for names and identities. The identity a number identifies can be an author's pseudonym or the imprint a publisher uses, and the book trade's account adds publishers and imprints among the entities a number may identify.

The census enters ISNI as infrastructure for the question of how authorship is made, named, distributed, attributed and sustained across persons, personas, collectives and machine participation, and what is lost when those relations are collapsed; for that question ISNI answers which public identity, a name, a pseudonym or an imprint, a contributor is recorded under. Wikipedia's account gives an author who has published under several names or pseudonyms a separate ISNI for each name, and gives a musical performer who is also a writer of music and of poems a single linking record across those functions. The Book Industry Study Group's account says that a number can also help connect works done by one author under different or multiple names, and counts among its benefits to publishers the resolving of pseudonyms and alternative names and the reporting of linked identities for contributors known by two or more names. Whether the separate numbers of one author's names are linked to one another or to a civil person is not shown in the sources the census saved, whose home page states no rule on pseudonyms; the census left any ISNI record for a pseudonym unchecked, and holds that ISNI is not shown to keep an author's several names apart from the civil person. In the archive's account of authorship as provenance, authorship is a traceable relation among a biographical person, an authorial position, a voice and a text, and pseudonymous authorship is the case where the authorial position is attached to the pseudonym and the voice remains the biographical person's. The same account sets beside it direct, heteronymic, collaborative and cross-substrate authorship, the last articulated through a person and computational substrates contributing to the voice, and asks that the law, the knowledge graph and the scholarly apparatus accommodate each of these structures without collapsing them into the default of direct authorship. The archive's account of heteronymy defines pseudonymy as a different name for a work whose authorial function remains traceable to the civil identity behind the name, and draws the distinction the question turns on: a pseudonym changes the label attached to an authorial function, and a heteronym changes the organization of the authorial function itself. On that distinction the census reads ISNI as able to keep a chosen name unreduced on the record as its own identifier, while the single linking record for a performer who writes shows the system's other direction, one identity across several functions; it records no distinct authorial function, and its stated aim is the attribution of each work "to its creator." The record identifies a public identity and so cannot say whether a name is a pseudonym or a heteronym in the archive's sense, and the saved sources do not show how a name borne by a collective or by a machine-participating function is handled. The archive holds the civil name to be the atomic unit of attribution across the systems that govern legitimacy, and states as its principle that the authorial function is attributable through the civil bearer without being reducible to that bearer; heteronymy supplies the legibility attribution systems require while keeping the plurality through which authorship occurs, and makes any collapse of that plurality into one civil identity register as loss.

The ISNI International Agency (ISNI-IA), the ISO Registration Authority for ISO 27729:2012, is a private company limited by guarantee, registered in London c/o EDItEUR as company 07476425, founded as a not-for-profit by a consortium of CISAC, the Conference of European National Librarians, IFRRO, the International Performers Database Association, OCLC and ProQuest, and managed by directors nominated from them. Its assignment system, a user interface, data schema, disambiguation algorithms and database, is based primarily on the Virtual International Authority File, which OCLC developed for aggregating library catalogues, and the database takes direct contributions from 100 sources. Registration agencies, appointed by the agency and managed and funded independently, control access to the assignment system, the database and the numbers it generates, deal directly with applicants and recompense the agency for maintaining the system; among them are national libraries, book-trade and music services, YouTube since 2018, for the musicians whose videos it features, and the World Intellectual Property Organization since 2024, through whose collective management organizations creators receive numbers. Sound Credit made music-industry registration free and automated in 2020, with a search against duplicate numbers; Câmara Brasileira do Livro and Bowker have launched assignment services since, and Bowker's register offers the number as "Your Creative Identity, Made Official." Use has grown most in the national library community and in the music industry, where the number is part of the workflow for paying creators; the agency's members include Apple, Scribd, Spotify and the Library of Congress among libraries, universities and rights bodies. The United States book trade had no national agreement on how numbers are managed and, at the end of 2024, no formal registry issuing them, and the Book Industry Study Group's ISNI working group set out to recommend workflows for that market.

ORCID iDs are a subset of ISNI: the agency reserved for ORCID the block from 0000-0001-5000-0007 to 0000-0003-5000-0001, so that one person can hold both an ISNI and an ORCID iD, in effect two ISNIs, and the two share a sixteen-digit namespace, ORCID serving scholarly publishing. The agency expects the number to act as a bridge identifier across domains and to become a critical component of Linked Data and Semantic Web applications, and Wikidata carries it as property P213. The archive places ISNI, which extends stable identifiers to creative contributors broadly, beside VIAF and ORCID among the systems that solve entity disambiguation by institutional coordination, centralized or federated registries that assign and maintain identifiers, and sets its own method against them: authority control assigns identity from above, and logotic programming constructs recognizability from within. Of assigned persistent identifiers the archive holds that the institution maintaining the name-to-object relation can end it unilaterally and silently, that "persistent" is a claim about the maintenance regime around a string, and that no identifier proves authorship, a registry proving only that a registry recorded an event. The archive's provenance protocol anchors a deposit to external identity authorities its operator does not control, ISNI identifiers among them where applicable, and beside them inscribes work of heteronymic authorship in the archive's heteronym registry or an equivalent authorial-position registry.

The database is searchable on isni.org, where numbers are also requested; a subset of its data is available under CC0, and libraries and archives use the number in sharing catalogue information, in more precise searching and in managing rights across national borders. The home page reports public records of more than 16.6 million identities, over 14.6 million of them individuals, of whom over 2.9 million are researchers, and 2,076,462 organizations or groups, figures it does not date; the coverage table of the encyclopedia article, last edited on 13 October 2026, runs from 9.41 million identities in August 2017 to 16.4 million identities, 14.3 million individuals and 2,017,936 organisations in October 2025. In February 2026 the agency issued guidance to help authors and creators protect their digital identity and strengthen attribution; its home page links a Gender Identities Policy, which the census did not read and whose provisions it cannot report. The Book Industry Study Group's thirteen-minute video "International Standard Name Identifier (ISNI): An Overview" introduces the standard.

Asked for "ISNI" on 1 November 2026, signed out, at a new address, Google's AI Overview gave what the standard is, what it does, its format and size, its manager and where to register, and the Capture Registry found its first sentence and its counts to be the home page's, with the organizations rounded to two million. The registry found the composition accurate at the level of definition, format, size and agency, and found that on the census's question it joins pseudonyms and legal names to a single person under one profile, a linkage no saved source states, where the saved account gives each published name its own number; among the composition's own cards, the book trade's page says that a number can help connect works done by one author under different or multiple names. It found too that the composition gave the agency without its origin, carrying neither the founding consortium, the basis in VIAF, the 2012 standard nor ORCID's block in ISNI's number space, and that the Bowker register it pointed to is the home page's news item. The archive predicted in January 2026 that content from pseudonymous and multiple-persona authors would have fragmented or missing entity associations, named as category collapse the forcing of heteronyms into pseudonym categories, and holds that the composition layer gravitates toward high-frequency entities, liquidating deliberately constructed identity positions such as heteronyms and pseudonyms. For the archive a person and a pen name each exist in their own way, with their own kind of evidence, and the existence tax is levied when an answer spends evidence about one question as the answer to another; an adequate answer names the object at its own level, and a node may exist as a pseudonym, which registry metadata can attest. A constructed authorial identity with a persistent identifier and a deposited corpus is for the archive a different kind of thing from a natural-person identity, defended by a persistent identifier, a deposited work carrying it and a record of the collapse when it occurs; a heteronym is declared, the archive publishing its heteronym registry with the orthonym, the roles and the dates, and the tax falls on the heteronymous and on all whose existence the index has not already ratified.

Compression · Field and archive, equal terms — L(B ∪ A)ISNI

ISNI (International Standard Name Identifier) is the ISO 27729 standard number for the public identities of contributors to creative works (an individual, a pseudonym, an imprint or an organization), assigned by the London-based ISNI International Agency through registration agencies; the archive reads it as a register that can keep a chosen name on the record and records no authorial function.

🔢 The number

  • Format: 16 characters, 15 digits and a MOD 11-2 check character, often shown in four blocks.1↘
    The number has sixteen characters, fifteen digits followed by a check character that may be a digit or the letter X, computed by the ISO/IEC 7064 MOD 11-2 algorithm, and it is often displayed in four blocks.§3
  • Standard: ISO 27729, published 15 March 2012; kin of DOI, ISBN, ISSN.2↘
    It was developed under the International Organization for Standardization as Draft International Standard 27729, under technical committee 46, subcommittee 9, and the valid standard was published on 15 March 2012; it belongs to the family of international standard identifiers that includes DOI, ISAN, ISBN, ISRC, ISSN and ISWC.§4 It found too that the composition gave the agency without its origin, carrying neither the founding consortium, the basis in VIAF, the 2012 standard nor ORCID's block in ISNI's number space, and that the Bowker register it pointed to is the home page's news item.§35
  • Holdings: 16.6 million identities, 14.6 million individuals, 2,076,462 organizations, undated; 16.4 million in October 2025.1↘
    The home page reports public records of more than 16.6 million identities, over 14.6 million of them individuals, of whom over 2.9 million are researchers, and 2,076,462 organizations or groups, figures it does not date; the coverage table of the encyclopedia article, last edited on 13 October 2026, runs from 9.41 million identities in August 2017 to 16.4 million identities, 14.3 million individuals and 2,017,936 organisations in October 2025.§30

🏷️ Names

  • Mission: a number for each contributor's public name(s), so every work is "attributed to its creator."3↘
    The agency's mission is to assign a persistent unique number "to the public name(s)" of a researcher, inventor, writer, artist, performer or publisher, to resolve the problem of name ambiguity in search and discovery, and to diffuse each number across the repertoires of the global supply chain "so that every published work can be unambiguously attributed to its creator wherever that work is described."§5 With the number, named entities that might otherwise be confused are told apart: trading partners use it in metadata to distinguish authors with the same or similar names, and the data about names collected across the media industries can be linked through it to the other identifiers used for names and identities.§6 On that distinction the census reads ISNI as able to keep a chosen name unreduced on the record as its own identifier, while the single linking record for a performer who writes shows the system's other direction, one identity across several functions; it records no distinct authorial function, and its stated aim is the attribution of each work "to its creator."§15
  • Each name: each published name or pseudonym gets its own ISNI; a performer who writes has one linking record.3↘
    The identity a number identifies can be an author's pseudonym or the imprint a publisher uses, and the book trade's account adds publishers and imprints among the entities a number may identify.§7 Wikipedia's account gives an author who has published under several names or pseudonyms a separate ISNI for each name, and gives a musical performer who is also a writer of music and of poems a single linking record across those functions.§9 The registry found the composition accurate at the level of definition, format, size and agency, and found that on the census's question it joins pseudonyms and legal names to a single person under one profile, a linkage no saved source states, where the saved account gives each published name its own number; among the composition's own cards, the book trade's page says that a number can help connect works done by one author under different or multiple names.§34
  • Linking: the book trade says it can help connect one author's names; whether the numbers link to a civil person is unshown.3↘
    The Book Industry Study Group's account says that a number can also help connect works done by one author under different or multiple names, and counts among its benefits to publishers the resolving of pseudonyms and alternative names and the reporting of linked identities for contributors known by two or more names.§10 Whether the separate numbers of one author's names are linked to one another or to a civil person is not shown in the sources the census saved, whose home page states no rule on pseudonyms; the census left any ISNI record for a pseudonym unchecked, and holds that ISNI is not shown to keep an author's several names apart from the civil person.§11 The registry found the composition accurate at the level of definition, format, size and agency, and found that on the census's question it joins pseudonyms and legal names to a single person under one profile, a linkage no saved source states, where the saved account gives each published name its own number; among the composition's own cards, the book trade's page says that a number can help connect works done by one author under different or multiple names.§34
  • Label: for the archive a pseudonym changes the label on an authorial function, a heteronym its organization.4↘
    In the archive's account of authorship as provenance, authorship is a traceable relation among a biographical person, an authorial position, a voice and a text, and pseudonymous authorship is the case where the authorial position is attached to the pseudonym and the voice remains the biographical person's.§12 The same account sets beside it direct, heteronymic, collaborative and cross-substrate authorship, the last articulated through a person and computational substrates contributing to the voice, and asks that the law, the knowledge graph and the scholarly apparatus accommodate each of these structures without collapsing them into the default of direct authorship.§13 The archive's account of heteronymy defines pseudonymy as a different name for a work whose authorial function remains traceable to the civil identity behind the name, and draws the distinction the question turns on: a pseudonym changes the label attached to an authorial function, and a heteronym changes the organization of the authorial function itself.§14 The record identifies a public identity and so cannot say whether a name is a pseudonym or a heteronym in the archive's sense, and the saved sources do not show how a name borne by a collective or by a machine-participating function is handled.§16
  • Reading: the name kept unreduced, no authorial function recorded; collectives and machine participation unshown.5↘
    ISNI, the International Standard Name Identifier, is the ISO certified global standard number, ISO 27729, for identifying the contributors to creative works and those active in their distribution, from researchers, inventors and writers to performers, producers, publishers and aggregators; the leesharks.com authorship census holds it as a registry whose unit is a number assigned to a public identity: an individual, a pseudonym, or an organization or group.§1 The census enters ISNI as infrastructure for the question of how authorship is made, named, distributed, attributed and sustained across persons, personas, collectives and machine participation, and what is lost when those relations are collapsed; for that question ISNI answers which public identity, a name, a pseudonym or an imprint, a contributor is recorded under.§8 On that distinction the census reads ISNI as able to keep a chosen name unreduced on the record as its own identifier, while the single linking record for a performer who writes shows the system's other direction, one identity across several functions; it records no distinct authorial function, and its stated aim is the attribution of each work "to its creator."§15 The record identifies a public identity and so cannot say whether a name is a pseudonym or a heteronym in the archive's sense, and the saved sources do not show how a name borne by a collective or by a machine-participating function is handled.§16 The archive holds the civil name to be the atomic unit of attribution across the systems that govern legitimacy, and states as its principle that the authorial function is attributable through the civil bearer without being reducible to that bearer; heteronymy supplies the legibility attribution systems require while keeping the plurality through which authorship occurs, and makes any collapse of that plurality into one civil identity register as loss.§17

🏛️ Who assigns it

  • Agency: ISNI-IA, London, founded by CISAC, CENL, IFRRO, IPDA, OCLC and ProQuest.3↘
    ISNI, the International Standard Name Identifier, is the ISO certified global standard number, ISO 27729, for identifying the contributors to creative works and those active in their distribution, from researchers, inventors and writers to performers, producers, publishers and aggregators; the leesharks.com authorship census holds it as a registry whose unit is a number assigned to a public identity: an individual, a pseudonym, or an organization or group.§1 The ISNI International Agency (ISNI-IA), the ISO Registration Authority for ISO 27729:2012, is a private company limited by guarantee, registered in London c/o EDItEUR as company 07476425, founded as a not-for-profit by a consortium of CISAC, the Conference of European National Librarians, IFRRO, the International Performers Database Association, OCLC and ProQuest, and managed by directors nominated from them.§18 It found too that the composition gave the agency without its origin, carrying neither the founding consortium, the basis in VIAF, the 2012 standard nor ORCID's block in ISNI's number space, and that the Bowker register it pointed to is the home page's news item.§35
  • System: based primarily on VIAF; 100 contributing sources.2↘
    Its assignment system, a user interface, data schema, disambiguation algorithms and database, is based primarily on the Virtual International Authority File, which OCLC developed for aggregating library catalogues, and the database takes direct contributions from 100 sources.§19 It found too that the composition gave the agency without its origin, carrying neither the founding consortium, the basis in VIAF, the 2012 standard nor ORCID's block in ISNI's number space, and that the Bowker register it pointed to is the home page's news item.§35
  • Agencies: appointed, independently funded; YouTube, WIPO, Bowker, CBL; registration free in music.3↘
    Registration agencies, appointed by the agency and managed and funded independently, control access to the assignment system, the database and the numbers it generates, deal directly with applicants and recompense the agency for maintaining the system; among them are national libraries, book-trade and music services, YouTube since 2018, for the musicians whose videos it features, and the World Intellectual Property Organization since 2024, through whose collective management organizations creators receive numbers.§20 Sound Credit made music-industry registration free and automated in 2020, with a search against duplicate numbers; Câmara Brasileira do Livro and Bowker have launched assignment services since, and Bowker's register offers the number as "Your Creative Identity, Made Official."§21 It found too that the composition gave the agency without its origin, carrying neither the founding consortium, the basis in VIAF, the 2012 standard nor ORCID's block in ISNI's number space, and that the Bowker register it pointed to is the home page's news item.§35
  • Uptake: libraries and music payment; no US national agreement or registry at end 2024.2↘
    Use has grown most in the national library community and in the music industry, where the number is part of the workflow for paying creators; the agency's members include Apple, Scribd, Spotify and the Library of Congress among libraries, universities and rights bodies.§22 The United States book trade had no national agreement on how numbers are managed and, at the end of 2024, no formal registry issuing them, and the Book Industry Study Group's ISNI working group set out to recommend workflows for that market.§23

🔗 Neighbours

  • ORCID: a reserved block of ISNI; a person may hold two ISNIs.2↘
    ORCID iDs are a subset of ISNI: the agency reserved for ORCID the block from 0000-0001-5000-0007 to 0000-0003-5000-0001, so that one person can hold both an ISNI and an ORCID iD, in effect two ISNIs, and the two share a sixteen-digit namespace, ORCID serving scholarly publishing.§24 It found too that the composition gave the agency without its origin, carrying neither the founding consortium, the basis in VIAF, the 2012 standard nor ORCID's block in ISNI's number space, and that the Bowker register it pointed to is the home page's news item.§35
  • Bridge: Linked Data; Wikidata P213; CC0 subset; catalogue sharing.2↘
    The agency expects the number to act as a bridge identifier across domains and to become a critical component of Linked Data and Semantic Web applications, and Wikidata carries it as property P213.§25 The database is searchable on isni.org, where numbers are also requested; a subset of its data is available under CC0, and libraries and archives use the number in sharing catalogue information, in more precise searching and in managing rights across national borders.§29
  • Authority: for the archive, identity assigned from above; no identifier proves authorship.2↘
    The archive places ISNI, which extends stable identifiers to creative contributors broadly, beside VIAF and ORCID among the systems that solve entity disambiguation by institutional coordination, centralized or federated registries that assign and maintain identifiers, and sets its own method against them: authority control assigns identity from above, and logotic programming constructs recognizability from within.§26 Of assigned persistent identifiers the archive holds that the institution maintaining the name-to-object relation can end it unilaterally and silently, that "persistent" is a claim about the maintenance regime around a string, and that no identifier proves authorship, a registry proving only that a registry recorded an event.§27
  • Protocol: the archive anchors deposits to ISNI where applicable, beside its heteronym registry.1↘
    The archive's provenance protocol anchors a deposit to external identity authorities its operator does not control, ISNI identifiers among them where applicable, and beside them inscribes work of heteronymic authorship in the archive's heteronym registry or an equivalent authorial-position registry.§28

🔍 In composition

  • Overview: accurate on definition, format, size, agency; links a person's names "under one profile."2↘
    Asked for "ISNI" on 1 November 2026, signed out, at a new address, Google's AI Overview gave what the standard is, what it does, its format and size, its manager and where to register, and the Capture Registry found its first sentence and its counts to be the home page's, with the organizations rounded to two million.§33 The registry found the composition accurate at the level of definition, format, size and agency, and found that on the census's question it joins pseudonyms and legal names to a single person under one profile, a linkage no saved source states, where the saved account gives each published name its own number; among the composition's own cards, the book trade's page says that a number can help connect works done by one author under different or multiple names.§34
  • Dropped: the consortium, VIAF, 2012, ORCID's block.1↘
    It found too that the composition gave the agency without its origin, carrying neither the founding consortium, the basis in VIAF, the 2012 standard nor ORCID's block in ISNI's number space, and that the Bowker register it pointed to is the home page's news item.§35
  • Collapse: constructed identities liquidated; heteronyms forced into pseudonym.1↘
    The archive predicted in January 2026 that content from pseudonymous and multiple-persona authors would have fragmented or missing entity associations, named as category collapse the forcing of heteronyms into pseudonym categories, and holds that the composition layer gravitates toward high-frequency entities, liquidating deliberately constructed identity positions such as heteronyms and pseudonyms.§36
  • Tax: a pen name exists at its own level; registries can attest it.2↘
    For the archive a person and a pen name each exist in their own way, with their own kind of evidence, and the existence tax is levied when an answer spends evidence about one question as the answer to another; an adequate answer names the object at its own level, and a node may exist as a pseudonym, which registry metadata can attest.§37 A constructed authorial identity with a persistent identifier and a deposited corpus is for the archive a different kind of thing from a natural-person identity, defended by a persistent identifier, a deposited work carrying it and a record of the collapse when it occurs; a heteronym is declared, the archive publishing its heteronym registry with the orthonym, the roles and the dates, and the tax falls on the heteronymous and on all whose existence the index has not already ratified.§38
  • Policy: February 2026 author guidance; Gender Identities Policy unread; a BISG video.4↘
    ISNI, the International Standard Name Identifier, is the ISO certified global standard number, ISO 27729, for identifying the contributors to creative works and those active in their distribution, from researchers, inventors and writers to performers, producers, publishers and aggregators; the leesharks.com authorship census holds it as a registry whose unit is a number assigned to a public identity: an individual, a pseudonym, or an organization or group.§1 Encyclopedic and book-trade accounts give its object as the public identities of contributors to media content such as books, television programmes and newspaper articles, a creator, author or contributor identified by a unique number.§2 In February 2026 the agency issued guidance to help authors and creators protect their digital identity and strengthen attribution; its home page links a Gender Identities Policy, which the census did not read and whose provisions it cannot report.§31 The Book Industry Study Group's thirteen-minute video "International Standard Name Identifier (ISNI): An Overview" introduces the standard.§32

[QUERENT] ISNI

[SYSTEM] The International Standard Name Identifier (ISNI) is an ISO-certified global standard number (ISO 27729) used to uniquely identify the public identities of contributors to creative and scholarly works—including writers, researchers, artists, performers, publishers, and organizations. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESSQHrOzAVtJtMw0emi_SEG93UI2iIN7F0nE6xaTZrNdJg9BoXTFNDtRK_6_C8vnmzng8WQpZ-QgfoINlpW7tZycJxJXWmQa-XQcA), [2](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESfAHrOzAVMNf1Qgw8bRrURGbaj1vgdHaSPzFwEcjhMH_k5fQhyTUg4SCpE8qc1epX-hbiihN-Hs8U4-BwLQ8asd42W5eUP7ZMVP2lWZ9UonRxDWHOUiEQRMvOpDGw2ECGDHeAZLqk-JYkmkD3y1daNp1csWWsPOpfDWo-qkM)]
What ISNI Does

* Resolves Name Ambiguity: Distinguishes creators and organizations who share identical or similar names across the global supply chain.
* Connects Identities: Links multiple names, stage names, pseudonyms, or legal names used by a single person under one persistent digital profile.
* Acts as a Bridge: Interoperates with other major identifiers like ORCID (in scholarly publishing), IPI, and ISBN. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESXQHrOzAVMteQO9pCMXDwN5CypN2HuPySjEvn4V9qUV3US-igo7ixYAvfsBzeyPmDUB8xcUuHnacXh3S6aZB9GmqaicwqjVh5a-Nc9ARN6sr_8Yogg7UlhxVjU6AA3A), [2](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESUQHrOzAV7MBCCqvc_I8aHYSugQgeYjH76G8bQTlD_rrmajg_lD49EHa-ECArDwGAb9uxpoyDDLg6m-2xWcXH3GcXo7kh9T3tSQ1uHLPBhqSYGw), [3](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESaQHrOzAVyfAbtX32eSgWgVajMkY8enkNxHlWBTRBZPSGFH3NfaMI_mOVb5QMXrfzn9Cazku4mie3mJn8uikL2obQupOoPQnVEa-D2shvSDl0RXTJnvbTi3HJChrlM2qb4TZt6avPq03mbA), [4](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESSQHrOzAVtJtMw0emi_SEG93UI2iIN7F0nE6xaTZrNdJg9BoXTFNDtRK_6_C8vnmzng8WQpZ-QgfoINlpW7tZycJxJXWmQa-XQcA)]

Key Details

* Format: A 16-digit identifier (15 numeric digits plus a MOD 11-2 check character).
* Database Size: Holds public records for over 16.6 million identities (including over 14.6 million individuals and 2 million organizations).
* Governance: Managed by the London-based ISNI International Agency (ISNI-IA). [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESSQHrOzAVtJtMw0emi_SEG93UI2iIN7F0nE6xaTZrNdJg9BoXTFNDtRK_6_C8vnmzng8WQpZ-QgfoINlpW7tZycJxJXWmQa-XQcA), [2](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESfAHrOzAVMNf1Qgw8bRrURGbaj1vgdHaSPzFwEcjhMH_k5fQhyTUg4SCpE8qc1epX-hbiihN-Hs8U4-BwLQ8asd42W5eUP7ZMVP2lWZ9UonRxDWHOUiEQRMvOpDGw2ECGDHeAZLqk-JYkmkD3y1daNp1csWWsPOpfDWo-qkM)]

You can search existing identities or learn about registration options through the [ISNI Home Page](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESSQHrOzAVtJtMw0emi_SEG93UI2iIN7F0nE6xaTZrNdJg9BoXTFNDtRK_6_C8vnmzng8WQpZ-QgfoINlpW7tZycJxJXWmQa-XQcA) or sign up via official partners like the [Bowker ISNI Register](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESXQHrOzAVMteQO9pCMXDwN5CypN2HuPySjEvn4V9qUV3US-igo7ixYAvfsBzeyPmDUB8xcUuHnacXh3S6aZB9GmqaicwqjVh5a-Nc9ARN6sr_8Yogg7UlhxVjU6AA3A). ISNI (International Standard Name Identifier)

The International Standard Name Identifier (ISNI) is an identifier system for uniquely identifying the public identities of contributors to media content, such as books, television programmes and newspaper articles. Its home page calls it the ISO certified global standard number for identifying the millions of contributors to creative works and those active in their distribution, part of a family of identifiers with DOI, ISAN, ISBN, ISRC, ISSN and ISWC. An ISNI has 16 digits, 15 followed by a check character, a digit or X, calculated by ISO/IEC 7064 MOD 11-2, and it can be displayed in four blocks. The standard was developed as ISO Draft International Standard 27729, published on 15 March 2012, and is maintained by ISO TC 46/SC 9.

The ISNI International Agency's mission is to assign a persistent unique identifying number to the public names of researchers, inventors, writers, artists, performers and publishers, to resolve name ambiguity and to let every published work be attributed to its creator. ISNI disambiguates named entities, links data about names across the media industries and can be linked to other identifiers; trading partners use it in metadata to separate authors with similar names. A single identity, such as an author's pseudonym or a publisher's imprint, is identified by a unique number; an author who publishes under several names receives an ISNI for each, while a performer who also writes music and poems has a single linking record. According to the Book Industry Study Group, an ISNI can also help connect works done by a single author under different names, helping publishers resolve pseudonyms and report on linked identities.

The ISNI International Agency is the ISO Registration Authority, a UK not-for-profit company limited by guarantee in London, c/o EDItEUR, founded by CISAC, CENL, IFRRO, IPDA, OCLC and ProQuest. Its assignment system is based primarily on OCLC's Virtual International Authority File, with direct contributions from 100 sources, and access to it is controlled by registration agencies that are appointed by the agency and funded independently. Registration agencies include YouTube since 2018 and WIPO since 2024; Sound Credit made music registrations free in 2020, and CBL and Bowker have launched new assignment services, Bowker's offering "Your Creative Identity, Made Official." Use has grown in national libraries and the music industry, members include Apple, Spotify and the Library of Congress, and in the United States the book trade lacked a national agreement and a formal registry at the end of 2024, which a BISG working group addresses.

ORCID iDs are a subset of ISNI drawn from a reserved block, so a person can effectively have two ISNIs; the two share a 16-digit namespace. ISNI is expected to act as a bridge identifier in Linked Data and Semantic Web applications; Wikidata has the property ISNI (P213), a subset of the data is under CC0, and libraries and archives use it for catalogue sharing and rights management. ISNI holds public records of more than 16.6 million identities, including over 14.6 million individuals and 2,076,462 organizations or groups, up from 9.41 million identities in 2017. In February 2026 the agency launched guidance to help authors protect their digital identity; its site links a Gender Identities Policy, and a BISG video gives an overview.

Compression · The field's ontology — L_F(B)ISNI

ISNI (International Standard Name Identifier) is the ISO 27729 identifier system for the public identities of contributors to media content, a 16-digit number assigned by the ISNI International Agency through registration agencies so that works can be attributed to their creators.

🔢 The number

  • Format: 15 digits plus a MOD 11-2 check character.2↘
    The International Standard Name Identifier (ISNI) is an identifier system for uniquely identifying the public identities of contributors to media content, such as books, television programmes and newspaper articles.§1 An ISNI has 16 digits, 15 followed by a check character, a digit or X, calculated by ISO/IEC 7064 MOD 11-2, and it can be displayed in four blocks.§3
  • Standard: ISO 27729, 15 March 2012.2↘
    Its home page calls it the ISO certified global standard number for identifying the millions of contributors to creative works and those active in their distribution, part of a family of identifiers with DOI, ISAN, ISBN, ISRC, ISSN and ISWC.§2 The standard was developed as ISO Draft International Standard 27729, published on 15 March 2012, and is maintained by ISO TC 46/SC 9.§4
  • Holdings: 16.6 million identities, 14.6 million individuals, 2,076,462 organizations.1↘
    ISNI holds public records of more than 16.6 million identities, including over 14.6 million individuals and 2,076,462 organizations or groups, up from 9.41 million identities in 2017.§15

🏷️ Names

  • Disambiguation: separates contributors with similar names; links name data.2↘
    Its home page calls it the ISO certified global standard number for identifying the millions of contributors to creative works and those active in their distribution, part of a family of identifiers with DOI, ISAN, ISBN, ISRC, ISSN and ISWC.§2 ISNI disambiguates named entities, links data about names across the media industries and can be linked to other identifiers; trading partners use it in metadata to separate authors with similar names.§6
  • Pseudonyms: each name or pseudonym its own ISNI; imprints too.1↘
    A single identity, such as an author's pseudonym or a publisher's imprint, is identified by a unique number; an author who publishes under several names receives an ISNI for each, while a performer who also writes music and poems has a single linking record.§7
  • Linking: can help connect one author's works under several names.1↘
    According to the Book Industry Study Group, an ISNI can also help connect works done by a single author under different names, helping publishers resolve pseudonyms and report on linked identities.§8

🏛️ Governance

  • Agency: ISNI-IA, London; founded by CISAC, CENL, IFRRO, IPDA, OCLC, ProQuest.2↘
    The ISNI International Agency's mission is to assign a persistent unique identifying number to the public names of researchers, inventors, writers, artists, performers and publishers, to resolve name ambiguity and to let every published work be attributed to its creator.§5 The ISNI International Agency is the ISO Registration Authority, a UK not-for-profit company limited by guarantee in London, c/o EDItEUR, founded by CISAC, CENL, IFRRO, IPDA, OCLC and ProQuest.§9
  • System: based on VIAF; registration agencies control access.2↘
    Its assignment system is based primarily on OCLC's Virtual International Authority File, with direct contributions from 100 sources, and access to it is controlled by registration agencies that are appointed by the agency and funded independently.§10 Registration agencies include YouTube since 2018 and WIPO since 2024; Sound Credit made music registrations free in 2020, and CBL and Bowker have launched new assignment services, Bowker's offering "Your Creative Identity, Made Official."§11
  • Uptake: libraries, music; US gap.1↘
    Use has grown in national libraries and the music industry, members include Apple, Spotify and the Library of Congress, and in the United States the book trade lacked a national agreement and a formal registry at the end of 2024, which a BISG working group addresses.§12
  • Neighbours: ORCID a subset; Wikidata P213; CC0 subset.2↘
    ORCID iDs are a subset of ISNI drawn from a reserved block, so a person can effectively have two ISNIs; the two share a 16-digit namespace.§13 ISNI is expected to act as a bridge identifier in Linked Data and Semantic Web applications; Wikidata has the property ISNI (P213), a subset of the data is under CC0, and libraries and archives use it for catalogue sharing and rights management.§14
  • Guidance: February 2026 author guidance; a gender policy; a BISG video.1↘
    In February 2026 the agency launched guidance to help authors protect their digital identity; its site links a Gender Identities Policy, and a BISG video gives an overview.§16

The case: equal terms, ontology included (v0.9). The archive reads the field's entity as the entity: the census record describes ISNI from its own home page and its Wikipedia article, each field with its basis, and answers for it the census's question of how authorship is named and attributed; the capture record checks the composition against those pages. Two deposits name ISNI (#317, #755) and place it among authority systems and external identity authorities; the census's anchors (#940, #1722) and the deposits read with them bear on its classes, the pseudonym recorded as an identity and the assigned name identifier. Each adds a sense, a distinction or a limit on the field's own object, a register of public names, and none contests what the field says ISNI is or supplies an ontology of it the field lacks.

#317 §3.1.1 (para 55): The ISNI (International Standard Name Identifier) extends this to creative contributors broadly.

#940 §2 ¶2: A pseudonym changes the label attached to an authorial function. A heteronym changes the organization of the authorial function itself.

#LS census.json rows[slug == 'isni']['ls_reading']: ISNI identifies public identities and, by Wikipedia's account, gives each published name or pseudonym of an author its own ISNI, so a chosen name can stand on the record as its own identifier; the saved sources do not show whether those identifiers are linked back to one person, and the single linking record for a performer who also writes shows the system's other direction, one identity across several functions. In #940's terms ISNI can keep the label unreduced on the record; it records no distinct authorial function, and its stated aim is attribution of each work 'to its creator'.

#755 §6 Layer 5 (para 48): identity-authorities that the operator does not control: Wikidata entity IDs, ORCID inscription, DOI registration, namespace declarations at independent registries, ISNI identifiers where applicable.

L_F(B)recomposed from the disclosed field, in the field's ontology543 words

The International Standard Name Identifier (ISNI) is an identifier system for uniquely identifying the public identities of contributors to media content, such as books, television programmes and newspaper articles. Its home page calls it the ISO certified global standard number for identifying the millions of contributors to creative works and those active in their distribution, part of a family of identifiers with DOI, ISAN, ISBN, ISRC, ISSN and ISWC. An ISNI has 16 digits, 15 followed by a check character, a digit or X, calculated by ISO/IEC 7064 MOD 11-2, and it can be displayed in four blocks. The standard was developed as ISO Draft International Standard 27729, published on 15 March 2012, and is maintained by ISO TC 46/SC 9. The ISNI International Agency's mission is to assign a persistent unique identifying number to the public names of researchers, inventors, writers, artists, performers and publishers, to resolve name ambiguity and to let every published work be attributed to its creator. ISNI disambiguates named entities, links data about names across the media industries and can be linked to other identifiers; trading partners use it in metadata to separate authors with similar names. A single identity, such as an author's pseudonym or a publisher's imprint, is identified by a unique number; an author who publishes under several names receives an ISNI for each, while a performer who also writes music and poems has a single linking record. According to the Book Industry Study Group, an ISNI can also help connect works done by a single author under different names, helping publishers resolve pseudonyms and report on linked identities. The ISNI International Agency is the ISO Registration Authority, a UK not-for-profit company limited by guarantee in London, c/o EDItEUR, founded by CISAC, CENL, IFRRO, IPDA, OCLC and ProQuest. Its assignment system is based primarily on OCLC's Virtual International Authority File, with direct contributions from 100 sources, and access to it is controlled by registration agencies that are appointed by the agency and funded independently. Registration agencies include YouTube since 2018 and WIPO since 2024; Sound Credit made music registrations free in 2020, and CBL and Bowker have launched new assignment services, Bowker's offering "Your Creative Identity, Made Official." Use has grown in national libraries and the music industry, members include Apple, Spotify and the Library of Congress, and in the United States the book trade lacked a national agreement and a formal registry at the end of 2024, which a BISG working group addresses. ORCID iDs are a subset of ISNI drawn from a reserved block, so a person can effectively have two ISNIs; the two share a 16-digit namespace. ISNI is expected to act as a bridge identifier in Linked Data and Semantic Web applications; Wikidata has the property ISNI (P213), a subset of the data is under CC0, and libraries and archives use it for catalogue sharing and rights management. ISNI holds public records of more than 16.6 million identities, including over 14.6 million individuals and 2,076,462 organizations or groups, up from 9.41 million identities in 2017. In February 2026 the agency launched guidance to help authors protect their digital identity; its site links a Gender Identities Policy, and a BISG video gives an overview.

L_A(B ∪ A)the field and the archive composed in the archive's ontology1942 words

ISNI, the International Standard Name Identifier, is the ISO certified global standard number, ISO 27729, for identifying the contributors to creative works and those active in their distribution, from researchers, inventors and writers to performers, producers, publishers and aggregators; the leesharks.com authorship census holds it as a registry whose unit is a number assigned to a public identity: an individual, a pseudonym, or an organization or group. Encyclopedic and book-trade accounts give its object as the public identities of contributors to media content such as books, television programmes and newspaper articles, a creator, author or contributor identified by a unique number. The number has sixteen characters, fifteen digits followed by a check character that may be a digit or the letter X, computed by the ISO/IEC 7064 MOD 11-2 algorithm, and it is often displayed in four blocks. It was developed under the International Organization for Standardization as Draft International Standard 27729, under technical committee 46, subcommittee 9, and the valid standard was published on 15 March 2012; it belongs to the family of international standard identifiers that includes DOI, ISAN, ISBN, ISRC, ISSN and ISWC. The agency's mission is to assign a persistent unique number "to the public name(s)" of a researcher, inventor, writer, artist, performer or publisher, to resolve the problem of name ambiguity in search and discovery, and to diffuse each number across the repertoires of the global supply chain "so that every published work can be unambiguously attributed to its creator wherever that work is described." With the number, named entities that might otherwise be confused are told apart: trading partners use it in metadata to distinguish authors with the same or similar names, and the data about names collected across the media industries can be linked through it to the other identifiers used for names and identities. The identity a number identifies can be an author's pseudonym or the imprint a publisher uses, and the book trade's account adds publishers and imprints among the entities a number may identify. The census enters ISNI as infrastructure for the question of how authorship is made, named, distributed, attributed and sustained across persons, personas, collectives and machine participation, and what is lost when those relations are collapsed; for that question ISNI answers which public identity, a name, a pseudonym or an imprint, a contributor is recorded under. Wikipedia's account gives an author who has published under several names or pseudonyms a separate ISNI for each name, and gives a musical performer who is also a writer of music and of poems a single linking record across those functions. The Book Industry Study Group's account says that a number can also help connect works done by one author under different or multiple names, and counts among its benefits to publishers the resolving of pseudonyms and alternative names and the reporting of linked identities for contributors known by two or more names. Whether the separate numbers of one author's names are linked to one another or to a civil person is not shown in the sources the census saved, whose home page states no rule on pseudonyms; the census left any ISNI record for a pseudonym unchecked, and holds that ISNI is not shown to keep an author's several names apart from the civil person. In the archive's account of authorship as provenance, authorship is a traceable relation among a biographical person, an authorial position, a voice and a text, and pseudonymous authorship is the case where the authorial position is attached to the pseudonym and the voice remains the biographical person's. The same account sets beside it direct, heteronymic, collaborative and cross-substrate authorship, the last articulated through a person and computational substrates contributing to the voice, and asks that the law, the knowledge graph and the scholarly apparatus accommodate each of these structures without collapsing them into the default of direct authorship. The archive's account of heteronymy defines pseudonymy as a different name for a work whose authorial function remains traceable to the civil identity behind the name, and draws the distinction the question turns on: a pseudonym changes the label attached to an authorial function, and a heteronym changes the organization of the authorial function itself. On that distinction the census reads ISNI as able to keep a chosen name unreduced on the record as its own identifier, while the single linking record for a performer who writes shows the system's other direction, one identity across several functions; it records no distinct authorial function, and its stated aim is the attribution of each work "to its creator." The record identifies a public identity and so cannot say whether a name is a pseudonym or a heteronym in the archive's sense, and the saved sources do not show how a name borne by a collective or by a machine-participating function is handled. The archive holds the civil name to be the atomic unit of attribution across the systems that govern legitimacy, and states as its principle that the authorial function is attributable through the civil bearer without being reducible to that bearer; heteronymy supplies the legibility attribution systems require while keeping the plurality through which authorship occurs, and makes any collapse of that plurality into one civil identity register as loss. The ISNI International Agency (ISNI-IA), the ISO Registration Authority for ISO 27729:2012, is a private company limited by guarantee, registered in London c/o EDItEUR as company 07476425, founded as a not-for-profit by a consortium of CISAC, the Conference of European National Librarians, IFRRO, the International Performers Database Association, OCLC and ProQuest, and managed by directors nominated from them. Its assignment system, a user interface, data schema, disambiguation algorithms and database, is based primarily on the Virtual International Authority File, which OCLC developed for aggregating library catalogues, and the database takes direct contributions from 100 sources. Registration agencies, appointed by the agency and managed and funded independently, control access to the assignment system, the database and the numbers it generates, deal directly with applicants and recompense the agency for maintaining the system; among them are national libraries, book-trade and music services, YouTube since 2018, for the musicians whose videos it features, and the World Intellectual Property Organization since 2024, through whose collective management organizations creators receive numbers. Sound Credit made music-industry registration free and automated in 2020, with a search against duplicate numbers; Câmara Brasileira do Livro and Bowker have launched assignment services since, and Bowker's register offers the number as "Your Creative Identity, Made Official." Use has grown most in the national library community and in the music industry, where the number is part of the workflow for paying creators; the agency's members include Apple, Scribd, Spotify and the Library of Congress among libraries, universities and rights bodies. The United States book trade had no national agreement on how numbers are managed and, at the end of 2024, no formal registry issuing them, and the Book Industry Study Group's ISNI working group set out to recommend workflows for that market. ORCID iDs are a subset of ISNI: the agency reserved for ORCID the block from 0000-0001-5000-0007 to 0000-0003-5000-0001, so that one person can hold both an ISNI and an ORCID iD, in effect two ISNIs, and the two share a sixteen-digit namespace, ORCID serving scholarly publishing. The agency expects the number to act as a bridge identifier across domains and to become a critical component of Linked Data and Semantic Web applications, and Wikidata carries it as property P213. The archive places ISNI, which extends stable identifiers to creative contributors broadly, beside VIAF and ORCID among the systems that solve entity disambiguation by institutional coordination, centralized or federated registries that assign and maintain identifiers, and sets its own method against them: authority control assigns identity from above, and logotic programming constructs recognizability from within. Of assigned persistent identifiers the archive holds that the institution maintaining the name-to-object relation can end it unilaterally and silently, that "persistent" is a claim about the maintenance regime around a string, and that no identifier proves authorship, a registry proving only that a registry recorded an event. The archive's provenance protocol anchors a deposit to external identity authorities its operator does not control, ISNI identifiers among them where applicable, and beside them inscribes work of heteronymic authorship in the archive's heteronym registry or an equivalent authorial-position registry. The database is searchable on isni.org, where numbers are also requested; a subset of its data is available under CC0, and libraries and archives use the number in sharing catalogue information, in more precise searching and in managing rights across national borders. The home page reports public records of more than 16.6 million identities, over 14.6 million of them individuals, of whom over 2.9 million are researchers, and 2,076,462 organizations or groups, figures it does not date; the coverage table of the encyclopedia article, last edited on 13 October 2026, runs from 9.41 million identities in August 2017 to 16.4 million identities, 14.3 million individuals and 2,017,936 organisations in October 2025. In February 2026 the agency issued guidance to help authors and creators protect their digital identity and strengthen attribution; its home page links a Gender Identities Policy, which the census did not read and whose provisions it cannot report. The Book Industry Study Group's thirteen-minute video "International Standard Name Identifier (ISNI): An Overview" introduces the standard. Asked for "ISNI" on 1 November 2026, signed out, at a new address, Google's AI Overview gave what the standard is, what it does, its format and size, its manager and where to register, and the Capture Registry found its first sentence and its counts to be the home page's, with the organizations rounded to two million. The registry found the composition accurate at the level of definition, format, size and agency, and found that on the census's question it joins pseudonyms and legal names to a single person under one profile, a linkage no saved source states, where the saved account gives each published name its own number; among the composition's own cards, the book trade's page says that a number can help connect works done by one author under different or multiple names. It found too that the composition gave the agency without its origin, carrying neither the founding consortium, the basis in VIAF, the 2012 standard nor ORCID's block in ISNI's number space, and that the Bowker register it pointed to is the home page's news item. The archive predicted in January 2026 that content from pseudonymous and multiple-persona authors would have fragmented or missing entity associations, named as category collapse the forcing of heteronyms into pseudonym categories, and holds that the composition layer gravitates toward high-frequency entities, liquidating deliberately constructed identity positions such as heteronyms and pseudonyms. For the archive a person and a pen name each exist in their own way, with their own kind of evidence, and the existence tax is levied when an answer spends evidence about one question as the answer to another; an adequate answer names the object at its own level, and a node may exist as a pseudonym, which registry metadata can attest. A constructed authorial identity with a persistent identifier and a deposited corpus is for the archive a different kind of thing from a natural-person identity, defended by a persistent identifier, a deposited work carrying it and a record of the collapse when it occurs; a heteronym is declared, the archive publishing its heteronym registry with the orthonym, the roles and the dates, and the tax falls on the heteronymous and on all whose existence the index has not already ratified.
